subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler — Latency & Throughput AB test follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Emma — great to meet today. Thanks for walking through Globex's inference priorities (low p95 for interactive features, predictable p99 for SLAs, and lowering per-token cost for high-volume batch jobs). Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Recap of today's asks:
  - Primary: reduce tail latency for customer-facing flows (p95/p99 targets)
  - Secondary: increase sustained tokens/sec for nightly batch summarization
  - Constraints: need to run tests against your baseline hyperscaler config (seq_len 512, batch size 16)

- What we committed to deliver by end of week:
  1) A/B test configuration and scripts (attached: redwood_abtest-config.yml)
  2) Initial comparative metrics (Redwood hosted vs your hyperscaler runs) with p95/p99 and tokens/sec
  3) Proposed next tests: dedicated-reserved run, cold vs warm KV cache, seq_len 1024 run

Attachments: redwood_abtest-config.yml (test harness), we'll consolidate results into a single CSV.

Proposed next step: can we schedule a 30-min sync for Thursday 10–10:30 PT to review the A/B results and agree on the production roll-forward criteria? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a brief runbook.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Quick clarifications before we run: 

1) Our hyperscaler team ran an initial baseline (attached: globex_hyperscaler_initial_run.csv) — numbers are cold-cache, seq_len 512. Can you confirm Redwood's test will match cold-cache conditions?
2) For p99, we need results over 10k requests to be meaningful — can your harness run that scale?

Also, curious on a couple of things we discussed: how does Redwood's smart routing behave under a regional outage? For this engagement we'll need a clear fallback plan and an SLA conversation (we can loop procurement later).

I'll take Thursday 10:00 PT. Please send invite.

—Emma

Globex Corporation

Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler — AB test config / internal ask

Marissa / Michael — copying internal infra folks to align on the run. Notes from my side: 

- Match Globex baseline: cold-cache, seq_len 512, batch 16 (we'll also run warm-cache after baseline).
- Metrics to capture (must appear in CSV): p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec sustained, GPU utilization, and 95th percentile throughput for concurrent clients.
- Initial Redwood-hosted numbers (local lab run, cold cache):
  - Redwood hosted (v1 runtime, fp16 quant): p95 = 180 ms, p99 = 320 ms, tokens/sec (sustained) = 2,500 tokens/sec
  - Hyperscaler baseline (provided by Globex): p95 = 340 ms, p99 = 620 ms, tokens/sec = 1,600 tokens/sec
  - Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, optimized batching): p95 = 150 ms, p99 = 260 ms, tokens/sec = 4,800 tokens/sec

Observations: Redwood shows materially lower tail latency and higher tokens/sec in our lab A/Bs, particularly when using dedicated capacity and persistent KV. The key reproducibility checks for Globex will be cold-cache parity and matching seq_len/batch.

Action items for infra: run 10k-request baseline for both Redwood hosted and Redwood Dedicated (if available), collect CSVs, and upload to the shared drive. Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stone <emma@globex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:07:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler — Latency & Throughput AB test follow-up

Emma — thanks for confirming Thursday. Sent calendar invite for Thu 10:00–10:30 PT. A few updates ahead of the call: 

- We've kicked off the 10k-request cold-cache baselines (attached: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_abtest_results.csv) for both Redwood hosted and Dedicated. Early summary: Redwood hosted p95/p99 and throughput are consistently better than the hyperscaler baseline in cold-cache runs; Dedicated further improves tokens/sec by ~2x. Full CSV attached.

- Regarding region/fallback: Redwood smart routing will fail over to a compatible model variant in a different region with automatic retries and circuit-breaker policies; we document the exact behavior and SLAs in our runbook. I'll bring a short slide on routing/fallback to Thursday's sync.

- Proposed test expansion (if Thursday looks good):
  1) Cold vs warm KV cache comparison (to see production delta)
  2) Seq_len 1024 A/B to surface cost/latency tradeoffs for longer context use cases
  3) Burst + sustained throughput test (48-hour run) on Dedicated if you want to validate billing/commit sizing

Let me know if you want Rafael or Michael to present any of the benchmark details on the call.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.
Marissa
